title: Retire Python, NumPy and JAX from active project architecture
summary: Human-governor requested retirement of Python, NumPy and JAX as active project languages/dependencies. This request does not directly modify the official Codex. It requires migration evidence for governance semantics, training, verification, model glue, dependency manifests and all production/runtime consumers before publication.
origin: human-governor directive: retire Python, NumPy and JAX

problem.summary: The active Codex currently permits Python governance semantics, JAX/NumPy training, and development verification. Current implementation still contains Python production paths, JAX/NumPy training paths, and Python package declarations. Full retirement cannot be certified without replacement implementations and parity evidence.
fail_closed_conditions: Any active Python production import remains
Any active NumPy or JAX import remains
Any Python/JAX/NumPy package remains in resident or optional manifests without an approved exception
Missing C/C++/Rust/C#/F# replacement contract or parity evidence
Missing training, governance, verification and rollback replacement evidence

LANGUAGES:C/C++/Rust/Go/CSharp/FSharp/JavaScript/SQL with Python, NumPy and JAX retired; training, governance semantics, verification, model glue, preprocessing, orchestration and fallback paths must be migrated to their registered owners before activation.

CORE-ORDER:correctness-first>declared-language-owner>reproducible-profile>contract parity>independent acceptance>certified activation; Python, JAX and NumPy are not eligible execution owners; every replacement requires bounded resources, cancellation, failure semantics, evidence and rollback.

PRIMARY-LANGUAGES:C23>C++23>C#14/F#10>Rust>Go>JavaScript; Python, NumPy and JAX are retired and may not remain in active dependency manifests, resident processes, request critical paths or training paths after certified migration.
